stages.title: Most frequent k

stages.require: Implement `TopKFrequent.Find(nums, k)` — most frequent first, ties by smaller value. k outside 0..distinct → `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. Better than O(n log n).

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given an array of integers and k, return the **k values that appear most often**, most frequent first.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Order of the result? (Most frequent first; ties by smaller value — so it can be tested.)
- Is k always valid? (Reject k larger than the number of distinct values.)
- Better than O(n log n)? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Count with a dictionary. A frequency is between 1 and n, so put each value into the bucket for its frequency and walk the buckets from the top. No comparison sort over all values: O(n).

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe count in a dictionary, drop each value into the bucket for its count, read buckets from the highest — O(n) time and memory. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Find concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Sorting all distinct values by count — O(d log d), what the question asks you to beat.
- Forgetting the tie rule, giving a non-deterministic answer.
- Bucket array of size max value instead of size n + 1.
